stories.headline: US Q4 GDP revised sharply down to 0.7% as government shutdown dragged growth

key_facts.fact: US GDP grew at an annualized rate of just 0.7% in Q4 2025, revised down from the initial estimate of 1.4% and well below the Dow Jones consensus forecast of 1.5%.
key_facts.excerpt: Gross domestic product, a measure of all the goods and services produced across the sprawling U.S. economy, rose at a seasonally and inflation-adjusted annual rate of just 0.7% in the fourth quarter.

key_facts.fact: The record 43-day government shutdown drove federal spending down 16.7%, subtracting 1.03 percentage points from overall growth.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. government shutdown late last year severely impacted economic growth, with federal spending and investment plunging at a 16.7% rate. That hacked 1.16 percentage points off fourth-quarter growth.

key_facts.fact: Core PCE inflation rose 0.4% in January and 3.1% on a 12-month basis, higher than the Federal Reserve's target, indicating cost pressures were building even before the Iran war.
key_facts.excerpt: The core PCE inflation rose 0.4% in January and 3.1% on a 12-month basis. The ex-food and energy reading was 0.1 percentage point higher than December.

key_facts.fact: For all of 2025, GDP posted a 2.1% increase, down from 2.8% in 2024. Exports declined 3.3%, the largest contraction since Q2 2023.
key_facts.excerpt: Exports declined at a faster pace of 3.3%, compared with the initial estimate of a 0.9% drop, marking the largest contraction since Q2 2023.

key_facts.fact: The GDP report was originally scheduled for February 26 but was delayed by the October-November 2025 government shutdown.
key_facts.excerpt: The second report for the fourth quarter of 2025, originally scheduled for February 26, 2026, was rescheduled due to the October–November 2025 government shutdown.

stories.headline: Goldman Sachs raises US recession probability to 25%, delays Fed rate cut forecast to September

key_facts.fact: Goldman Sachs raised its 12-month US recession probability to 25%, up 5 percentage points from its previous estimate, citing the Iran war's impact on oil prices.
key_facts.excerpt: Revised forecasts show 25% recession probability by Q3 2026, with unemployment rising to 4.6% and core PCE inflation peaking at 2.7%.

key_facts.fact: Goldman pushed back its forecast for the first Fed rate cut from June to September 2026, with a second cut expected in December, warning that oil-driven inflation could delay monetary easing.
key_facts.excerpt: Goldman has pushed back its expectation for the first Fed rate cut from June to September, warning that a significant oil shock could reignite inflation, dampen growth, and trigger a stock market sell-off.

key_facts.fact: Goldman revised its headline PCE inflation forecast for Q4 2026 from 2.1% to 2.9%, and its GDP growth forecast from 2.5% to 2.2%. In an extreme oil scenario ($145/bbl), GDP growth could fall to 1.9%.
key_facts.excerpt: Goldman expects the December 2026 headline Personal Consumption Expenditure index at 2.9%, up from its previous forecast of 2.1%.

key_facts.fact: Goldman estimates a sustained 10% increase in oil prices lifts headline PCE inflation by 0.2 percentage points and shaves 0.1 pp off GDP growth.
key_facts.excerpt: A sustained 10% increase in oil prices lifts headline PCE inflation by 0.2 pp and core PCE by 0.04 pp, while shaving about 0.1 pp off GDP growth.

stories.headline: Trump launches trade probes against dozens of countries to replace $1.6T in tariff revenue

key_facts.fact: The Supreme Court struck down Trump's emergency tariffs on February 20, 2026, eliminating approximately $1.6 trillion in expected tariff revenue over the next decade according to the CBO.
key_facts.excerpt: The Trump administration this week stepped up its ambitious effort to replace about $1.6 trillion in lost tariff revenue that was eliminated by the Supreme Court's decision to strike down a range of the president's import taxes.

key_facts.fact: Trump launched unfair trade practice investigations into dozens of countries including allies like Canada, Mexico, the UK, and the EU, covering excess industrial capacity and forced labor compliance.
key_facts.excerpt: The Trump administration has launched unfair trade practices investigations into dozens of countries. The probes will look into everything from excess industrial capacity to whether other countries are doing enough to combat forced labor.

key_facts.fact: Trump now relies on Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act, which requires longer processes including public hearings and industry comment. A factory capacity investigation hearing is set for May 5, and a forced labor hearing for April 28.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump is now relying on Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act, which requires longer, more complex processes including consultations with targeted countries, public hearings, and industry commentary.

key_facts.fact: A temporary 10% tariff on all imports was imposed under separate legal authority for 150 days, with the potential to raise it to 15%.
key_facts.excerpt: He also imposed a temporary 10% tariff on all imports under separate legal authority, lasting 150 days (with potential to raise to 15%).

stories.headline: Brent crude closes at $103 as IEA calls Hormuz crisis 'largest oil disruption in history'

key_facts.fact: Brent crude rose 2.67% to close at $103.14/bbl on March 13, the highest in over three years. US WTI crude settled at $98.71/bbl, up 3.11%.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent futures rose 2.67%, or $2.68, to close at $103.14 per barrel. U.S. crude oil gained 3.11%, or $2.98, to settle at $98.71 per barrel.

key_facts.fact: The IEA characterized the Hormuz crisis as 'the largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market' and agreed to release a record 400 million barrels from strategic stockpiles, with the US contributing 172 million barrels.
key_facts.excerpt: The war in the Middle East is creating the largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market.

key_facts.fact: The US issued a second 30-day sanctions waiver for Russian oil loaded before March 12, broader than the initial India-only directive. Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev said it would free up an estimated 100 million barrels.
key_facts.excerpt: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced on Thursday the temporary waiver of sanctions on Russian oil and petroleum products for a period of 30 days. Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev said the move would free up for buyers an estimated 100 million bbl of Russian oil.

key_facts.fact: Trump is considering suspending the Jones Act to allow non-American tankers to transport energy between domestic ports, as the Hormuz blockade has idled hundreds of vessels and sent charter rates soaring.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump said Friday he was considering suspending the Jones Act to allow non-American tankers to transport energy and agricultural products between local ports amid a squeeze in vessel availability.

key_facts.fact: Gas prices have risen 65 cents per gallon since the war began, with the national average climbing rapidly.
key_facts.excerpt: Americans acutely feeling the pain at the pump, the national price for a gallon of gas is up 65 cents just since the war with Iran began.

stories.headline: IMO warns 3,000 ships and 20,000 sailors stranded in Persian Gulf in worst maritime crisis since WWII

key_facts.fact: The International Maritime Organization warned that over 3,000 commercial vessels and 20,000 seafarers remain stranded in the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman, the largest maritime disruption since World War II.
key_facts.excerpt: The International Maritime Organization warned on Friday that more than 3,000 commercial vessels and 20,000 seafarers remain stranded across the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman, marking the largest maritime disruption since the Second World War.

key_facts.fact: At least 17 vessels have been attacked in key Middle East shipping lanes over the past two weeks, with at least one Indian national killed, according to UKMTO data.
key_facts.excerpt: At least 17 vessels have been attacked in key Middle East shipping lanes over the past two weeks amid the ongoing conflict, according to a report by CNN citing data from the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).

key_facts.fact: Some 15,000 cruise passengers are among those stranded. The trapped vessels include grain carriers and oil tankers, with shipping through the Strait of Hormuz collapsed to a fraction of pre-war volume.
key_facts.excerpt: Among the trapped vessels are grain carriers... 15,000 cruise passengers stranded.

key_facts.fact: Iran selectively allowed a Turkish vessel (Rozana) and two Indian tankers (Pushpak and Parimal) to pass through the strait on March 13, among the first approved crossings during the crisis.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran allowed the vessel Rozana (Turkish Flag) to pass through the Strait of Hormuz on 13 March 2026, making it one of the first approved crossings during the crisis.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia intercepts 51 Iranian drones including over Riyadh; Oman reports 2 killed

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia intercepted and destroyed 51 drones across the kingdom on March 13, including over Riyadh and the Eastern Province, in one of the largest coordinated aerial attacks since the war began.
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi Arabia said it intercepted and destroyed 51 drones across the kingdom, including in Riyadh, on Friday.

key_facts.fact: Oman reported two drone crashes in Sohar killing two foreign citizens and injuring others. Dubai and Abu Dhabi reported interception debris and safety alerts; no injuries in Dubai.
key_facts.excerpt: Oman reported two drone crashes in Sohar, killing two foreign citizens and injuring others. Dubai and Abu Dhabi reported interception debris and safety alerts.

key_facts.fact: UAE Minister of State Lana Nusseibeh said 'the extent of the attacks came as a shock,' vowing the Emirates would 'bounce back.'
key_facts.excerpt: The extent of the attacks came as a shock, UAE Minister of State Lana Nusseibeh said, vowing the Emirates would 'bounce back.'

key_facts.fact: Iran's IRGC warned that UAE ports Jebel Ali and Khalifa are 'next legitimate targets,' while Iran's FM called on Gulf nations to expel US forces.

stories.headline: Afghanistan retaliates with drone strikes on Pakistan's Kohat military base as conflict escalates

key_facts.fact: Afghanistan conducted retaliatory drone strikes on Pakistan Army installations in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on March 13, significantly damaging the Kohat Military Fort, a war command centre along the Durand Line.
key_facts.excerpt: Afghanistan conducted retaliatory drone strikes on strategic military centres and installations of the Pakistan Army in the Kohat area. Pakistan's Kohat Military Fort, a war command centre along the Durand Line, and the office of the fort's commander sustained significant damage.

key_facts.fact: Pakistan had struck the fuel depot of private airline Kam Air near Kandahar Airport, which supplies fuel to civilian airlines and UN aircraft, along with the Taliban's 313 Corps headquarters in Kabul and camps in Paktia and Kandahar.
key_facts.excerpt: Pakistan has bombed the fuel depot of private airline Kam Air near Afghanistan's Kandahar airport. The company supplies fuel to civilian airlines as well as to United Nations aircraft.

key_facts.fact: Pakistan's airstrikes killed women and children as civilian homes were targeted, according to Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid, who warned the aggression would 'not go unanswered.'
key_facts.excerpt: Pakistan also carried out bombings in other areas, including the capital Kabul, with women and children among those killed as civilian homes were targeted.

key_facts.fact: Pakistan's Defence Minister Khawaja Asif declared 'open war' on Afghanistan, stating the 'cup of patience has overflowed.' The conflict reportedly has US backing.
key_facts.excerpt: Pakistan's Defense Minister, Khawaja Asif, announced Islamabad's decision to wage war on Afghanistan. Islamabad's operations, reportedly enjoying international backing including from the U.S.

stories.headline: Qatar helium shutdown from Iranian drone strikes puts semiconductor supply chain on two-week clock

key_facts.fact: QatarEnergy's Ras Laffan facility, responsible for nearly a third of global helium supply, has been offline since March 2 following Iranian drone strikes. QatarEnergy declared force majeure on March 4.
key_facts.excerpt: QatarEnergy declared force majeure on existing contracts on March 4, freeing it from supply obligations to customers.

key_facts.fact: Helium consultant Phil Kornbluth warned that if the outage extends beyond two weeks, distributors would be forced to relocate cryogenic equipment and revalidate supplier relationships — a process stretching months.
key_facts.excerpt: Helium consultant Phil Kornbluth, speaking at a Gasworld webinar on March 4, said that if the outage extends beyond roughly two weeks, industrial gas distributors could be forced to relocate cryogenic equipment and revalidate supplier relationships.

key_facts.fact: South Korea sourced 64.7% of its helium from Qatar in 2025 and is among the most exposed countries. Seoul's Ministry of Trade opened a review of 14 critical supply items.
key_facts.excerpt: South Korea is among the most exposed countries, which, according to the Korea International Trade Association, imported 64.7% of its helium from Qatar in 2025.

key_facts.fact: Helium is essential for cooling silicon wafers during chip fabrication and has no effective substitute. The halted Qatari output removed an estimated 5 million cubic meters of monthly helium from the global market.
key_facts.excerpt: Helium prices surged after Qatar halted liquefied natural gas production this week, removing an estimated 5 million cubic meters of monthly helium output from the global market.

stories.headline: YolTech gets FDA clearance for in vivo gene-editing therapy YOLT-202 targeting Alpha-1 deficiency

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved YolTech Therapeutics' IND application for YOLT-202, an in vivo adenine base-editing therapy that corrects the PiZ mutation to PiM in Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency (AATD), enabling a Phase 2/3 clinical trial.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the Investigational New Drug (IND) application for YOLT-202, the company's investigational in vivo base-editing therapy for the treatment of Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency (AATD).

key_facts.fact: In a first-in-human trial with two patients, YOLT-202 showed rapid dose-dependent AAT level increases by Week 1, with the 45mg dose achieving normal range (>20 μM) with >95% corrected M-AAT protein.
key_facts.excerpt: The 45 mg dose group achieved normal range (>20 μM) with >95% corrected M-AAT protein. The newly produced proteins were both structurally corrected and functional.

key_facts.fact: CEO Yuxuan Wu characterized YOLT-202 as a potential 'one and done' therapy. The drug previously received Orphan Drug Designation from the FDA.
key_facts.excerpt: CEO Yuxuan Wu characterized it as potential 'one and done' therapy. YOLT-202 previously received Orphan Drug Designation from the FDA.

key_facts.fact: The Phase 2/3 study will be an open-label, single-dose multiregional clinical trial across US and international sites for adult patients with AATD.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA approval enables the initiation of an open-label, single-dose expansion Phase 2/3 clinical study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of YOLT-202 in adult patients with Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency.

sources.title: YolTech Therapeutics Receives FDA Clearance to Initiate Phase 2/3 Study of In Vivo Gene-Editing Therapy YOLT-202 in Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency (AATD)
